findings.message: getHtml returns Quill 2's internal `root.innerHTML` rather than `getSemanticHTML()`, so the email gets Quill's editor-only markup. With Quill 2.0.3, a user makes a bullet list. Quill stores it as `<ol><li data-list="bullet">`, and HtmlSanitizer strips `data-*` attributes, so recipients get a numbered list. Code blocks (`div.ql-code-block`) and class-based indent/alignment (`ql-indent-1`) are also lost. Turndown has the same problem when switching to Markdown.

`client.GetFolder(SpecialFolder.Sent)` throws NotSupportedException on servers without SPECIAL-USE/XLIST, so the `?? GetFoldersAsync(...)` fallback never runs. The IMAP server lacks SPECIAL-USE but has a plain "Sent" folder. GetFolder throws, the outer catch logs a warning, and the sent message is never saved, even though the fallback was written for exactly this case.

Minimal APIs don't check the DataAnnotations on SendMailRequest (Program.cs has no AddValidation), so null `To`, `Subject` or `Body` reach the code without being checked. POST `{"mailboxId":"...","subject":"x","body":"y","contentType":"plain"}` without `to`: `request.To.Length` throws NullReferenceException → 500. A null `subject` makes `message.Subject = null` throw ArgumentNullException inside the service → 500 instead of 400. ContentType/StringLength limits are also not enforced.

Only InvalidOperationException is caught and it is always mapped to 'MailboxNotFound'. SMTP/auth/decrypt failures are not handled, and MailKit's ServiceNotConnected/ServiceNotAuthenticated exceptions (subclasses of InvalidOperationException) get mislabeled. Wrong SMTP password → AuthenticationException → unhandled 500. Recipient rejected → SmtpCommandException → 500. Keys rotated → CryptographicException from Unprotect → 500. A MailKit connection-state InvalidOperationException → 404 'Mailbox not found' for a mailbox that exists.

setHtml writes `root.innerHTML` directly instead of going through Quill (`clipboard.convert`/`setContents` or `dangerouslyPasteHTML`), so marked's `<ul>`/`<pre>` output doesn't go through Quill's blot normalization. Switch from Markdown with a bullet list or fenced code block back to Rich Text. The raw `<ul>`/`<pre><code>` is put in the editor without Quill's model, so it gets mangled or reverted on the next edit, and getText/isEmpty can disagree with what is shown.
